stock.fillHint: Fill in the «Counted» column only — the variance and its value are calculated for you. Any sale made after the snapshot time above is not reflected here.
stock.poolLine: Pooled section stock (not split across barcodes)
stock.poolStatus: Pooled — value is an estimate at the section's average prices
stock.g1: Print the «Count sheet» or open it on a tablet, and walk the shelves in the company/section order it is sorted by.
stock.g2: Type what you counted by hand into the yellow «Counted» column — it is the only column you write in.
stock.g3: «Variance» and «Variance value» are calculated automatically. Negative is a shortage, positive is a surplus.
stock.g4: The «Summary» sheet adds it up as you type: how many lines were counted, how many are left, and the value of shortages and surpluses.
stock.g5: Blue rows are pooled stock for a whole section that was never split across barcodes — its value is an estimate at the section's average prices.
stock.gvSnap: These figures are a picture of the stock at the time printed at the top of the sheet. Any sale after that shows up as a variance caused by timing, not by loss — pause selling during the count, or subtract the period's sales.
stock.gvBarcode: Stored as text on purpose so Excel does not turn them into scientific notation and eat leading zeros. Do not change the column format to «Number».
stock.gvPrices: Written at full precision with no rounding — so the variance value matches reality to the last fraction.
stock.gvId: The last column is the product's ID in the system. Do not edit it; it is what matches a row to its product when two names look alike.
stock.gvFreeze: To keep the header row visible while scrolling: View tab → Freeze Panes → Freeze Top Row.
